entries.description: Register.

Extend the `docs/modules.yaml` entry shape with the fields tiers 5–7 need — `codeRoots`, `specSections`, `contextAssets` — additively, so entries written by today's `modules.py` stay valid and the extension keeps rendering them. Reject an unknown key rather than ignoring it.

Add `context_scope.py`: given a diff and a module slug, resolve the seven tiers and return a structured scope. Tiers 1–3 carry full content; tier 4 carries interface surface only, extracted by parsing rather than by asking a model, one hop, comments excluded; tiers 5–6 come from the manifest; tier 7 is names only. Everything unmatched is excluded, and the scope records what it excluded and why — an exclusion nobody can see is indistinguishable from a bug.

Fold `prompting.py` into `route.py` and replace the silent tail-truncation with a refusal that names the overrun, the budget, and the module-scoping remedy. Assert in a test that no code path returns a silently truncated prompt.
Cross-provider verification through `copilot-cli`.
Required portion of the full test suite.
Close-out.
Registered session 1 (copilot).
Extended the docs/modules.yaml entry shape with codeRoots, specSections and contextAssets; unknown keys are rejected, entries written by the old writer stay valid.
Added context_scope.py: seven tiers resolved mechanically -- 1-4 bounded by the change, 5-7 by the module -- with every exclusion recorded and its reason.
Folded prompting.py into route.py and replaced the silent tail-truncation with PromptTooLargeError naming the overrun, the budget and the module-scoping remedy; prompting.py deleted.

Cross-provider verification through copilot-cli: 3 rounds, each finding a distinct real defect, each remediated -- r1 tier 4 blind to extensionless TS imports (gpt-5.5/openai); r2 the TS extractor kept bodies and dropped contracts (gemini-3.1-pro-preview/google); r3 code contradicted the locked spec, resolved by an operator-directed spec amendment (gpt-5.5/openai). Round cap reached; r3 finding 0 disputed on the record; adjudication unavailable (every seat provider had already participated); operator attested the waiver at an interactive prompt.

Full Python suite green: 449 passed in 140s, against the 480-test ceiling (414 before this session; +35 for the manifest validation, the seven-tier scope, the prompt-size refusal, and the truncation false-positive).
Closed WAIVED: five gates green, work committed as d5d1b782 and pushed. Verdict is the operator waiver on round 3 finding 0, adjudication having been unavailable.
Register.

Make the scope the evidence builder for module-mapped sessions: `verify.py` builds from `context_scope` when the set declares a module that resolves in the manifest, and from today's monolithic bundle when it does not. The round-1 / fix-delta distinction is unchanged.

Render the scope so the verifier knows what it was and was not given: each tier labelled, tier 4 visibly marked interface-or-full, tier 7 visibly names-only, and an explicit statement that everything else is excluded by default and what the domain is. A verifier that does not know its context is bounded will confabulate the rest.

Add the two-step pull. An **in-domain request** names a file the scope already listed and is served mechanically — no justification, because nothing needs to weigh it. An **escalation** names a file outside the domain and says why; the **orchestrating engine** decides, with no human in the loop, and may only widen. Both are logged as ledger rows naming the file, the outcome, and the decider. A wildcard or unnamed request is refused, and the refusal says what a valid request looks like. A refusal never licenses abstention: the verifier returns a verdict on the evidence it holds, and "my escalation was refused" is not a verdict.
Cross-provider verification through `copilot-cli`.
Required portion of the full test suite.
Close-out.
Registered session 2 (copilot).

verify.py builds round-1 evidence from context_scope when the set's spec declares a module that resolves in docs/modules.yaml, and from the monolithic bundle when it does not; round-1/fix-delta distinction unchanged.

render_scope labels every tier, marks tier 4 interface-or-full per file, marks tier 7 names-only, names tier 2 as regex-found candidates rather than a call graph, records every exclusion, and states the domain.

In-domain requests served mechanically with one bounded re-dispatch; out-of-domain escalations recorded pending and decided by the orchestrating engine via verify grant/refuse. Every request, refusal and decision is a pulls.jsonl row naming file, outcome and decider.

VERIFIED round 1 by gpt-5.5/openai over copilot-cli, orchestrator provider anthropic excluded. The round also exercised the new fork live: the set declares module 'default', docs/modules.yaml does not carry it, and the run announced the fallback to the unscoped bundle and named the remedy.
143 targeted tests green across tests/test_verify.py, test_ledger.py, test_session.py, test_context_scope.py and the new test_context_pull.py (26). Repo total 475 against the 480 ceiling.
Five gates green; session 2 closed VERIFIED and pushed.
